thread:
maya-ops: paging — hosted inference p95/p99 spike, queue growing fast. getting alerts from frontdoor and queued-request meter. consumers seeing 30s+ latencies.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: #INC-2027-1223 — Hosted API high queue depth (sev-2) — paging maya-ops

maya-ops: i'm on it. initial ask: confirm backlog size and affected model(s). ryan-sre can you pull queue metrics?

ryan-sre: grabbing queue snapshot now. current total queued requests: 48k, rate in ~2.1k req/s sustained for last 3m. p95 token latency spiked from 200ms -> 6s, p99 ~23s. autoscaler showing repeated scale attempts failing: hitting GPU quota + scale negotiation timeouts.

sophia-eng: which models are hot? looks like text-generation-v2 and a few customer pinned variants — v2-65b on dedicated pools is saturated.

eli-ml: looks like traffic spike originated from a marketing campaign hitting a handful of tenants with heavy chat sessions (long prompts + streaming). also a lot of requests with long max_tokens.

maya-ops: customer-impact check — customer-success, please list top affected tenants and revenue critical ones.

customer-success: affected list (top 5 by QPS): acme-corp (prod), novella-ai (prod), shoplane (staging), partner-x (prod), research-lab (dev). acme and partner-x high priority. contacting acme now.

ryan-sre: autoscaler logs show repeated "scale-up rejected: capacity constraint" from provider API (403 QuotaExceeded). internal cluster pool tried to create 12 nodes, 9 rejected. fallback path attempted to use bursting pool, but bursting pool reached concurrent model instance limit. stack: runtime-batch-queue -> serving-pool-manager -> autoscaler.

eli-ml: in addition, KV-cache worker threads are backlog bound. continuous batching is coalescing many long-session requests, increasing per-batch memory and preventing fast scheduling.

maya-ops: mitigation plan (short list): 1) reduce incoming acceptance -> enable permissive rate-limiter to shed low-priority traffic 2) fail-fast for oversized max_tokens 3) enable smaller model fallback for public tier 4) request emergency quota bump + manual node creation 5) stop continuous batching for affected models (force small batch sizes).

sophia-eng: i'm toggling rate-limit policy to 50% for non-enterprise keys and setting token cap to 1024 for now. applying in 30s.

ryan-sre: done — policy applied. new ingress shows accept rate down ~48%. queue growth slowed but still ~15k queued.

eli-ml: enabling fallback routing to text-embed-lite for streaming-heavy customers? that will change quality. propose fallback to v2-6b quantized for non-enterprise.

maya-ops: go ahead with 6b fallback for non-enterprise. sophia, put note in response headers so clients see degraded-mode.

sophia-eng: adding header X-Redwood-Degraded: true. routing rules updated.

incbot: NOTE: manual scale requested (region us-west2) by ryan-sre. Provider request id: req-9b3f. Status: pending.

ryan-sre: provider responding with ETA ~12-15m for quota approval. manual node creation attempt partially succeeded — 3 GPU nodes added, but kube controller failed to schedule model pods due to insufficient GPU drivers on nodes (ami drift). investigating.

eli-ml: we can hack a temporary workaround: re-image nodes with correct runtime AMI and restart kubelet -> schedule pods. need someone with infra access.

maya-ops: ryan take infra runway, i'll coordinate customer comms. eli/sophia do runtime config changes for batch sizing and backpressure.

ryan-sre: re-imaging in progress. ETA 8m.

sophia-eng: forced batch-size cap applied for text-generation-v2: max_batch_tokens=4096 and batch_timeout=30ms. turning off continuous_batching for the model instance groups.

eli-ml: also set KV cache TTL to 30s for those instances to reduce memory pressure.

customer-success: update for acme-corp: they reported 40% of requests timing out. i've opened emergency support ticket and offered temporary degraded fallback.

maya-ops: customer comms: standard line — "We've detected a traffic surge causing degraded response times for some hosted endpoints. We're applying throttling and fallback measures; enterprise customers unaffected after fallback. We'll provide postmortem." keep it short.

incbot: Incident status changed to "mitigating" — add updates in-thread.

ryan-sre: re-image completed, kube pods now scheduling. added 6 new model instances across v2-6b and v2-13b quantized pools. queued requests draining. current queued ~6.8k, p95 down to 1.1s, p99 ~4.8s.

eli-ml: quality impact: fallback to 6b will increase perplexity on some prompts; but acceptable for most low-priority customers. suggesting a throttling rule to protect core enterprise keys so they get full model.

sophia-eng: throttle rule already whitelists enterprise keys. enterprise p95 stable ~280ms.

maya-ops: ask: do we keep continuous batch disabled for 30m to avoid re-coalescing? eli recommend yes.

eli-ml: yes keep disabled. can re-enable after traffic normalizes and we've validated node health.

ryan-sre: provider quota bumped (emergency approve). we added 10 more nodes; cluster capacity looks healthy. autoscaler now shows healthy decisions.

incbot: Reminder: 1h on-call handoff scheduled at 1800 UTC. maya-ops to handoff to ryan-sre.

maya-ops: prepping handoff notes: summary, mitigation steps taken, follow-ups, customer list. handoff in 10m.

customer-success: acme-corp confirmed degraded fallback acceptable for now. keeping ticket open for SLA credit discussion.

sophia-eng: infra follow-up: create an image validation pipeline to prevent AMI drift causing kube scheduling failures again. filing a task in infra backlog.

eli-ml: tuning follow-up: add adaptive batch-size strategy to avoid continuous-batch blowouts with long-session skews. will draft RFC.

maya-ops: post-incident items: 1) add explicit quota-alert (provider rejected scale-up) to paging triggers, 2) add quick-fallback routing for high-length requests, 3) document runbook for re-imaging nodes under pressure, 4) ensure customer communication templates include fallback notice.

ryan-sre: logs/diagnostics saved to s3://incidents/1771234567/ and linked to the incident ticket.

incbot: Incident status changed to "resolved" — last update: p95/p99 back to acceptable levels, queue drained, manual mitigations in place. Please file postmortem within 72h.

maya-ops: closing thread here. thanks all.

sophia-eng: thumbs up.

eli-ml: nice work.

ryan-sre: +1

customer-success: will follow up with customers.
